renderings.value: Expresses the idea of 'no matter how... or', 'even if... or'.

The ～うが ～うが grammar pattern is used to express that regardless of the conditions in A and B, the result remains the same. Often you’ll see volitional forms or i-adjective '-かろうが' forms. It can be translated as 'no matter how... or...', 'even if... or...'.
Verb-volitional form + うが + Verb-volitional form + うが, or Adjective (-かろう) + が + Adjective (-かろう) + が
A うが B うが: no matter whether A or B. Same as うと～うと.
No matter whether it's early morning or late at night, the bus is always late.
Even if I talk to him or don't, the outcome won't change.
Whether I do this job or not, the salary is the same.
I don't think that person would understand whether I talk to them or not.
